title: Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 — Rules and Regulations, 2011, Penalties
shortDescription: The statute, the 2011 Rules and Regulations, the enforcement hierarchy and the penalty ladder — heavily examined.
genZNote: Section numbers are boring until they're easy freebies. Learn the penalty ladder from 'extraneous matter' all the way to 'unsafe food' — it's the plot of this chapter.

sections.heading: Objectives and Principles
sections.body: The FSS Act, 2006 (enforced August 2011) aims to consolidate food laws, establish FSSAI, set science-based standards and regulate manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import. Section 18 states the guiding principles: risk analysis, precaution where evidence is incomplete, transparency and consumer protection. Section 26 makes the Food Business Operator responsible for compliance; Section 27 fixes liability of manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers.

sections.heading: Rules and Regulations, 2011
bullets: FSS Rules, 2011 — procedural: adjudication, appeals, sampling, prosecution, Food Safety Appellate Tribunal.
Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses Regulations, 2011.
Food Products Standards and Food Additives Regulations, 2011 — standards for dairy, cereals, meat, fats, beverages and additives.
Packaging and Labelling Regulations, 2011 (later replaced by Labelling & Display Regulations, 2020 and Packaging Regulations, 2018).
Prohibition and Restriction on Sales Regulations, 2011; Contaminants, Toxins and Residues Regulations, 2011; Laboratory and Sample Analysis Regulations, 2011.

table.caption: Authorities under the Act
rows: Head of state food-safety administration; prohibits/orders in public interest
Issues/cancels licences, ensures sampling, sanctions prosecution
Inspects, draws samples, seizes, sends to Food Analyst
Food Safety Appellate Tribunal (s.70); High Court

sections.heading: Penalty Ladder (approximate maxima)
sections.body: Regulatory details change by notification; treat figures here as exam-standard knowledge and confirm against the current FSSAI/Gazette text before relying on them professionally.

table.caption: Selected penalties
rows: Failure to comply with FSO directions (s.55)
Up to ₹2 lakh / up to ₹10 lakh
Up to 6 months (no injury) … up to 6 years (grievous injury); death: minimum 7 years to life and fine not less than ₹10 lakh

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The FSS Act, 2006 is the principal statute creating FSSAI and a risk-based framework of standards, licensing, enforcement and graded penalties for food businesses.
keyFacts: Operational August 2011 with Rules and Regulations, 2011.
s.26: FBO responsible; s.27 liability chain; s.18 risk analysis.
s.59 unsafe food is the gravest offence; death → life imprisonment possible.
Adjudicating Officer is of ADM rank.

highYieldFacts: Order: FSO samples → Food Analyst → Designated Officer → prosecution/adjudication.
Hazardous adulterant penalty up to ₹10 lakh (s.57).
commonTraps: Do not confuse FSO (field officer) with Designated Officer (licensing and prosecution sanction).
Do not give older PFA Act penalties for FSS Act offences.
mustRemember: s.30 Commissioner; s.36 Designated Officer; s.37 FSO; s.68 Adjudicating Officer; s.70 Tribunal.

confusedTerms.distinction: FSO samples and inspects; Designated Officer licenses, reviews reports and sanctions prosecution.

possibleQuestions: Define unsafe food and state the maximum punishment where death results.
